rationale: While evidence from Parenti et al. (18 individuals) and Peng et al. confirms that pathogenic MAU2 variants cause Cornelia de Lange syndrome 7 (CdLS7) with variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance of craniofacial signs (such as absence of synophrys and thick eyebrows in Peng et al.), the hypothesis that this distinguishes MAU2 from NIPBL/classical CdLS on the assumption of >95% synophrys penetrance is contradicted by clinical cohort data. Notably, Liu et al. (2020) reported synophrys in only 40% (4/10) of Chinese CdLS patients, the majority of whom harbored NIPBL mutations (70%), demonstrating that synophrys penetrance can be markedly lower than 95% in non-European or heterogeneous cohorts. Furthermore, the precise 50-65% (10-12/18) range for MAU2 is constrained by the limited total number of reported cases worldwide.

evidence.text: Parenti et al. characterized 18 individuals carrying 15 heterozygous MAU2 variants, identifying variable expressivity ranging from classic CdLS to milder presentations, with craniofacial traits such as synophrys and arched/thick eyebrows being enriched in the classic CdLS subgroup but not universally present across all affected individuals.

conflicts: The hypothesis assumes classic NIPBL-related CdLS has >95% penetrance for synophrys; however, Liu et al. (2020) demonstrated synophrys in only 40% (4/10) of Chinese CdLS patients despite 70% of the cohort carrying NIPBL variants.

While thick/arched eyebrows and synophrys are established as cardinal features in classical CdLS, individual MAU2-CdLS7 case descriptions (e.g., Peng et al., 2024) document total absence of both synophrys and bushy eyebrows, confirming that clinical discrimination cannot rely on intermediate penetrance estimates derived from small single-cohort assessments.

new_directions.question_text: Does the presence or absence of synophrys in MAU2-CdLS7 correlate with the specific functional class of MAU2 variant (in-frame missense disrupting NIPBL interaction vs truncating haploinsufficiency)?
new_directions.rationale: Parenti et al. documented two distinct molecular mechanisms and two distinct episignatures for MAU2 variants; evaluating facial dysmorphism penetrance by episignature group will clarify phenotypic expressivity.

new_directions.question_text: What is the sensitivity and specificity of objective 3D facial photogrammetry in differentiating MAU2-related CdLS7 from other non-NIPBL cohesinopathies (e.g., SMC1A, SMC3, RAD21, HDAC8)?
new_directions.rationale: Because manual phenotypic scoring of eyebrows and synophrys exhibits variable inter-observer penetrance and population variation, computer-aided facial gestalt analysis may provide definitive distinguishing metrics.
